targets.from: judgement values from the drafter's reading of the sources and knowledge of the species (2026-11-04), no photographs measured; to be replaced by photo measurements: a low, flat-topped, rigid mound much wider than tall, pale grey-green with whitish spiny twigs

description: A low, flat-topped, spiny shrub knee- to waist-high and spreading wide, its stiff, pale grey-white twigs ending in sharp thorns and set with small grey-green three-veined leaves. It forms dense mounds in open pine and fir forest, on burns and on dry flats and ridges, about 1500-3000 m, and covers itself with fragrant white flower clusters in early summer.

season_notes.winter: Evergreen and buried under snow, which it is shaped to carry; pale stems show where it melts out.
season_notes.spring: Fresh grey-green leaves as the snow goes; deer browse the new shoots.
season_notes.summer: Foamy white, honey-scented flower clusters, June-July, then small sticky capsules.
season_notes.fall: The capsules split and fling their seeds, which can wait in the soil for a century for a fire.

range.where: open pine and red fir forest, burns, dry flats and ridges: Crane Flat to White Wolf, Glacier Point Road, the Tioga Road

notes: Lower, flatter and paler than buckbrush (the template), with spine-tipped grey-white twigs that make the whole mound look frosted, and leaves with three veins from the base. FEIS: an important browse and a major part of mule deer diet on Sierra summer ranges; long-eared chipmunks cache its seed, pocket gophers eat it, birds and small mammals take the fruit, dusky-footed woodrats nest in it (none of these but the deer in the library; mountain quail stands in for the seed-eating birds). It thrives on burns and logged ground and also grows under giant sequoias. Flowering May-August, about 23 days per plant (FEIS); months here are for the Yosemite high country, the drafter's estimate. FEIS range 650-3350 m.
